title: Skill erosion, individual memory and the reversibility of AI adoption
abstract: arXiv:2611.04886v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Generative AI can improve immediate performance but may erode the human skills needed for future work. We consider a population of agents who perform a task either with their own skill or with the help of AI. Agents tend to imitate more successful peers, and their skills evolve in time: improving with practice and eroding with reliance on AI. We study, analytically and with simulations, the collective consequences of AI adoption. We show that the mechanism of skill erosion makes adoption bistable and that   the long-term behaviour of the population depends on how skills are distributed: populations with the same adoption and mean skill can reach opposite asymptotic states, depending on how expertise is shared between AI users and non-users. A deterministic description that follows the mean skills of the two groups and the variance of skills among non-users predicts the outcome of individual runs as accurately as the simulations allow

translated_title: 技能侵蚀、个体记忆与AI采用的可逆性
translated_abstract: 生成式AI可以提高即时表现，但可能会侵蚀未来工作所需的人类技能。我们考虑一个由智能体组成的群体，它们要么凭借自身技能执行任务，要么借助AI完成任务。智能体倾向于模仿更成功的同伴，其技能随时间演化：随练习而提升，随对AI的依赖而退化。我们通过解析分析和模拟研究了AI采用的集体后果。我们表明，技能侵蚀机制使AI采用呈现双稳态，且群体的长期行为取决于技能的分布方式：具有相同采用率和平均技能水平的群体可能达到截然相反的渐近状态，这取决于专业知识在AI使用者与非使用者之间如何分配。一个追踪两组平均技能以及非使用者群体中技能方差的确定性描述，能够达到与模拟相同的精度来预测个体运行的结果。
tldr: 该研究揭示了技能侵蚀机制使AI采用呈现双稳态，即使群体具有相同的采用率和平均技能水平，也可能因技能在AI使用者与非使用者之间的分布差异而走向截然相反的长期结局。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that skill erosion makes AI adoption bistable, meaning populations with identical adoption rates and mean skill levels can converge to opposite long-term outcomes depending solely on how expertise is distributed between AI users and non-users.
